questions.stem: What does the term NewSQL refer to?
options: A single database product sold by one vendor
A class of modern relational database management systems designed to meet the performance and scalability needs of modern applications
A new version of the SQL language that replaces SELECT statements
A category of document-oriented NoSQL databases
A file format for exchanging data between spreadsheets
questions.explanation: NewSQL refers to a class of modern relational database management systems designed for the performance and scalability requirements of modern applications, particularly in distributed and cloud environments.

questions.stem: What potential benefit is suggested if the NewSQL model materialises?
options: Eliminating the need for separate SQL and NoSQL datastores, saving significant effort
Removing the need for any database administrators
Making all data publicly available by default
Replacing cloud computing with on-premises servers
Eliminating the need for data backups
questions.explanation: If NewSQL materialises, it has the potential to streamline operations by eliminating the need for separate SQL and NoSQL datastores.

questions.stem: What do the letters in ACID stand for?
options: Access, Control, Integration, Deployment
Availability, Capacity, Indexing, Distribution
Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability
Analysis, Compression, Iteration, Design
Authentication, Confidentiality, Integrity, Detection
questions.explanation: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability, properties that NewSQL databases maintain to ensure data integrity.

questions.stem: How do NewSQL databases achieve scalability?
options: By buying a single much larger server
By reducing the amount of data stored
By dropping SQL support entirely
By scaling horizontally, adding more nodes to a distributed system
By limiting the number of concurrent users
questions.explanation: NewSQL databases are designed to scale horizontally, handling increasing workloads by adding more nodes to a distributed system.

questions.stem: Why does SQL compatibility matter for NewSQL databases?
options: It prevents the database from running in the cloud
It forces developers to learn a new query language
It makes the database slower but more secure
It removes the need for ACID compliance
It makes it easier for developers to transition from traditional relational databases
questions.explanation: NewSQL databases support traditional SQL queries, making it easier for developers to move from traditional relational databases to these newer systems.

questions.stem: Which of these is given as an example of a NewSQL database?
options: Google Spanner
Microsoft Excel
Apache Kafka
MongoDB Atlas
Oracle Forms
questions.explanation: Google Spanner, a globally distributed and horizontally scalable database system, is one of the NewSQL examples given, alongside CockroachDB and NuoDB.

options: A proprietary desktop spreadsheet tool
An open-source, distributed SQL database designed to be scalable, resilient and strongly consistent
A streaming platform for video delivery
A metadata registry standard
A programming language for data science
questions.explanation: CockroachDB is described as an open-source, distributed SQL database designed to be scalable, resilient and strongly consistent.

questions.stem: Which architectural designs may NewSQL databases use to distribute data and workload across nodes?
options: Monolithic and single-server architectures
Mainframe and terminal architectures
Distributed and shared-nothing architectures
Peer-to-peer file-sharing architectures
Client-only architectures with no server
questions.explanation: NewSQL databases may use innovative designs such as distributed and shared-nothing architectures to spread data and workload across multiple nodes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a key characteristic attributed to NewSQL databases?
options: Horizontal scalability
High performance for read and write operations
ACID compliance
Abandoning structured query language in favour of key-value access only
SQL compatibility
questions.explanation: NewSQL databases keep SQL support and ACID compliance while adding scalability and performance; abandoning SQL is the opposite of their aim.

questions.stem: Is NewSQL tied to a specific product or technology?
options: Yes, it is the trademark of a single company
Yes, it refers only to Google Spanner
Yes, it is a specific version of PostgreSQL
Yes, it is a cloud service sold by one provider
No, it represents a category of databases that share similar goals and characteristics
questions.explanation: The term NewSQL is not associated with a specific technology or product but represents a category of databases sharing similar goals and characteristics.
